## 8. Clear/lifecycle race

A previously untested angle was found while criticizing the single-flight design:
`clear()` could otherwise allow an already-running build to repopulate the cache after
the caller explicitly cleared it.

V1.41 adds a cache generation:

```text
clear()
  ↓
generation += 1
  ↓
active pre-clear build finishes
  ↓
result returned to its current waiters
  ↓
result NOT stored in the cleared cache
```

New callers after the clear do not join the pre-clear in-flight registry.

This is covered by an explicit regression test.

## 9. Locking / performance design

The cache `RLock` protects only:

- LRU entries;
- statistics;
- flight ownership metadata.

The lock is never held while arbitrary resolver work executes.

Different fingerprints therefore remain independently buildable.

A two-key barrier test confirmed peak simultaneous builders = 2.

## 10. Memory pressure

Real cached `ResolvedComponent` instances were measured recursively:

| distinct results | one result deep bytes | cache-entry graph deep bytes |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5,773 | 6,222 |
| 10 | 5,773 | 35,435 |
| 100 | 5,773 | 331,201 |
| 1,000 | 5,773 | 3,277,941 |

The measurements are fixture-specific Python object estimates. They do not justify a
new byte-budget cache policy yet. Entry-count LRU remains the current bounded policy.

## 11. Sequential performance sanity check

Latest local measurement:

- cold resolution: approximately **303,241 ns**;
- warm median hit: approximately **129,957 ns**;
- 1 miss / 1 store / 100 hits.

These are local engineering timings, not production performance certification.

## 12. Frame/scene hand-off

No production frame or scene consumer currently owns a `ResolutionCache`.

A caller-owned hand-off test explicitly reused one cache across two compiled graph
instances representing two frame boundaries:

```text
frame 1 graph → resolve → MISS/store
frame 2 graph.rebuild() → resolve → HIT/same object
```

No global ownership was added.

Because there is no actual frame/scene cache consumer, no `get_or_build_for_graph()` API
was introduced.

## 13. Cross-surface dependency regression

The post-change audit reproduces V1.40's partition:

| mutation | resolution | geometry |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| visual-only | changed | unchanged |
| relation topology | changed | changed |
| relation effect metadata only | changed | unchanged |

Single-flight does not alter any fingerprint dependency.

## 14. Statistics / telemetry decision

`ResolutionCacheStats` remains an immutable snapshot.

No `reset()` was added and no telemetry field was added because:

1. statistics snapshots already isolate observation windows;
2. there is no production cache consumer requiring centralized telemetry;
3. single-flight correctness is observable through deterministic runtime probes.

## 15. COLOR boundary

No production color runtime file changed:

- `runtime/effect_color.py` — unchanged;
- `runtime/effects.py` — unchanged;
- `runtime/color_spaces.py` — unchanged.

`RESOLUTION_VERSION` remains `20` because fingerprint/resolution semantics did not change.

The board contains:
